card.summary_ko: 1923년 조선물산장려회가 발표한 취지서. 의식주를 외국·일본 제품에 의존하는 현실이 민족의 생존을 위협한다고 보고, 조선 사람이 만든 물건을 사 쓰자고 호소한다.
card.summary_en: The 1923 prospectus of the Joseon Products Promotion Society. It argues that depending on foreign and Japanese goods for food, clothing and shelter threatens the nation's survival, and urges Koreans to buy and use goods made by Koreans.
card.edition_ko: 위키문헌 「조선물산장려회취지서」, 판 350168, 전사: 위키문헌 기여자, CC BY-SA 4.0 (1923년 단체 문서; 원문은 띄어쓰기 없이 전사됨)
card.edition_en: Korean Wikisource, 'Prospectus of the Joseon Products Promotion Society', revision 350168, transcription by Wikisource contributors, CC BY-SA 4.0 (a 1923 group document; the source is transcribed without word spacing)

notes.ko:
**저자 / 발행 주체** 조선물산장려회라는 단체의 취지서로, 기초한 개인은 분명히 알려져 있지 않다. 이 운동은 1920년 평양에서 조만식 등이 조선물산장려회를 만든 데서 시작해, 1922~1923년 서울에서 조선청년회연합회를 중심으로 확대된 것으로 알려져 있다. 조만식(1883~1950)은 기독교 신자이자 오산학교 교장을 지낸 비폭력·자립 노선의 민족주의 우파(부르주아 민족주의, 흔히 '조선의 간디'로 불림)이며, 해방 후 북한에서 조선민주당을 이끌다 소련군정과 충돌해 연금되었고 1950년 사망했다. 이 운동은 민족 자본가와 기독교·천도교계 민족주의자가 주도했다고 평가되며, 사회주의자들은 이를 '자본가의 이익을 위한 운동'이라 비판했다.

**시대적 맥락** 1919년 3·1운동 후 일제는 이른바 '문화통치'로 정책을 바꾸었다. 1920년대 초 민족 안에서는 실력양성론(교육·산업 진흥)이 힘을 얻었고, 같은 시기에 민립대학 설립 운동도 일어났다. 1923년 서울 조선물산장려회는 '내 살림 내 것으로'라는 구호를 내세웠다. 그러나 가격 상승으로 오히려 가난한 소비자가 부담을 졌고, 사회주의 계열은 상인·자본가의 이익을 지켜 줄 뿐이라고 비판했으며, 운동은 1920년대 중반 이후 약해졌다. 1930년대 초에 다시 시도되었으나 일제 말기에 사라졌다고 한다.

**배경** 1923년(계해년) 초에 발표되었다. 이 취지서에는 '음력 계해 정월 1일(양력 1923년 2월 16일)'부터 실행한다는 조항이 있다. 위키문헌 전사본은 띄어쓰기가 없는 국한문혼용체이다.

**의의** 일제강점기 경제적 민족운동의 대표적 선언이다. '의식주 문제'를 정치적 권리와 이어 놓고, 부자와 가난한 사람 모두에게 이해가 걸려 있다고 설득하는 논법이 특징이며, 실력양성론의 한계와 사회주의와의 갈등을 보여 주는 자료이기도 하다.

**형식과 주제** 하나의 긴 서문 단락과 실행 조건 세 조항으로 이루어진다. 수사 의문문('~리오')과 반복(의식주, 생활, 생명, 인격)이 많고, 부자와 가난한 사람의 가상 대화가 설득의 핵심이다. 원문의 '삼람'(사람) 같은 오자는 그대로 두었다.

**읽기 도움**
- 依支(의지): 의지하다. 産業的 基礎: 산업의 기초.
- 몸뚱이: 몸을 속되게 이르는 말.
- 굴헝텅이: 구렁텅이.
- 如前히: 전과 같이. 獎勵: 장려.
- 周衣(주의): 두루마기. 裳: 치마.
- 癸亥: 1923년. 又난: '又는'(또는).
- 'ᄯ', 'ᄭ' 같은 된소리 합자가 쓰였다(예: ᄯᅩ, ᄯᅡᆼ).
notes.en:
**About the issuing body** The prospectus of an organisation, the Joseon Products Promotion Society; the individual drafter is not clearly known. The movement is generally said to have begun in Pyongyang in 1920, when Cho Man-sik and others founded a Joseon Products Promotion Society, and to have spread in 1922-23 in Seoul, centred on the Korean Youth Association Federation. Cho Man-sik (1883-1950), a Christian and principal of Osan School, was a right-leaning bourgeois nationalist with a non-violent, self-reliance line, often called the "Gandhi of Joseon"; after liberation he led the Korean Democratic Party in the North, clashed with the Soviet authorities, was placed under house arrest, and died in 1950. The movement is regarded as led by national capitalists and by Christian and Cheondogyo nationalists, and socialists criticised it as a movement for the benefit of capitalists.

**Historical context** After the March First Movement of 1919 the Japanese colonial regime shifted to the so-called "cultural rule". In the early 1920s the "self-strengthening" idea (education and industry first) gained strength among nationalists, and a movement to found a people's university arose at the same time. In 1923 the Seoul society used the slogan "our living from our own goods". But prices rose, so poorer consumers bore the burden; socialists criticised it as protecting merchants and capitalists; and the movement faded after the mid-1920s. It was reportedly attempted again in the early 1930s but disappeared in the last years of the colonial period.

**Background** Issued in early 1923 (the year Gye-hae). The prospectus includes a rule that the measures begin on the first day of the lunar first month of Gye-hae (16 February 1923 by the Gregorian calendar). The Wikisource transcription is in mixed script without word spacing.

**Significance** A representative declaration of the economic wing of the colonial-period national movement. It links the question of food, clothing and shelter to political rights and tries to persuade both rich and poor that their interests are at stake, and it also shows both the limits of the self-strengthening approach and its conflict with socialism.

**Form and themes** One long preamble paragraph followed by three implementation conditions. It uses many rhetorical questions (-리오) and repetition (food, clothing, shelter; life, existence, dignity), and the imagined speech of a rich man and a poor man is its main persuasive device. Misprints such as 삼람 (for 사람) are left as in the source.

**Reading help**
- 依支 (의지): to depend on. 産業的 基礎: industrial foundation.
- 몸뚱이: vulgar word for "body".
- 굴헝텅이: standard 구렁텅이, "pit".
- 如前히: as before. 獎勵: encouragement.
- 周衣: traditional overcoat (durumagi). 裳: skirt.
- 癸亥: the year 1923. 又난: 又는, "or".
- Old tense-consonant clusters are used (e.g. ᄯᅩ, ᄯᅡᆼ).

paragraphs.en: If we have nothing to eat, nothing to wear, and nothing to depend on for our living, our life will be destroyed. What rights, freedom or happiness can we expect then, and how can we hope for any truly human development? The first condition of our life is food, clothing and shelter, that is, the industrial foundation. If this industrial foundation is destroyed and nothing is left to us, is it not only natural that we, having nothing at all, can neither live a human life as human beings nor achieve a human development? For this reason the most urgent question for us is that of food, clothing and shelter, that is, the question of industry. Then what is the position of the Joseon people today with regard to this question? We shall not cite statistics of various kinds; but look at the clothes we wear, look at the food we eat, and look at all the articles we use. Which of them was made by our own hands, or produced by our own strength? Are they not all things that others made, which we bought by selling our own bodies, and go on buying and using? If, in this way, we sell even our houses, our land and our bodies to pay for all the articles we use and receive supplies from the hands of others, can we still go on living as before, attached to our own land and keeping our houses? If, when the industrial foundation is destroyed, our life, our existence and our dignity are inevitably destroyed with it, then we say that this economic condition of the Joseon people drives all of us Joseon people into the pit of destruction. Some rich man may say: "I am a man with money and a man with land; it has nothing to do with me." But what is to be done when that land and that money gradually disappear and, on the contrary, debts and hardship grow? And some poor man may say: "I am a man who never had money and has no land; whether the Joseon people perish and others grow rich, or others perish and we Joseon people grow rich, what has that to do with us?" But in reality, what is to be done about the misfortune of losing one's job and having one's farmland taken away simply because one is a Joseon person, so that one wanders the roads with no way to keep oneself alive? Rich or poor, unless we hold in our own hands the right to industry, the first condition of life, we can never hope for our life, our dignity, or the development of our society. Standing on this view, in order to encourage the products of the Joseon people we take as our aims: first, that Joseon people buy and use what Joseon people have made; and second, that Joseon people unite and themselves make and supply the articles they use. Without such resolve and such effort, how could the Joseon people maintain their livelihood and develop their society?
Conditions for Implementation in the First Period

paragraphs.orig: 一. 衣服은爲先男子는周衣女子는裳(치마)을陰曆癸亥正月一日로부터朝鮮人産品又난加工品을染色하야着用할일
paragraphs.modern: 一. 衣服은 爲先 男子는 周衣 女子는 裳(치마)을 陰曆 癸亥 正月 一日로부터 朝鮮人 産品 又는 加工品을 染色하여 着用할 일
paragraphs.en: 1. As for clothing, to begin with, men are to wear the coat (jubui) and women the skirt (chima), dyed and made from Joseon-made goods or processed goods, from the first day of the first month of the lunar year Gye-hae.

paragraphs.orig: 一. 飮食物에對하야는食鹽, 砂糖, 果物淸凉飮料等을除한外는全혀朝鮮人産物을使用할일
paragraphs.modern: 一. 飮食物에 對하여는 食鹽, 砂糖, 果物 淸凉飮料 等을 除한 外는 全혀 朝鮮人 産物을 使用할 일
paragraphs.en: 2. As for food and drink, apart from salt, sugar, fruit, soft drinks and the like, Joseon-made products are to be used entirely.

paragraphs.orig: 一. 日用品은朝鮮人製品으로代用키可能한것은此를使用할일
paragraphs.modern: 一. 日用品은 朝鮮人 製品으로 代用키 可能한 것은 此를 使用할 일
paragraphs.en: 3. As for daily necessities, Joseon-made goods are to be used wherever they can be substituted.
